summary: Keep the unstopped mechanical gate runners in a trigger-kept table so the reconciler's list stops parsing every gate request in history

replay.detail: No claim replay changes. The explicit projection rebuild refills the table from the claims and marks the copy complete.

schema.detail: New local tables local_gate_runners (one row per exec, loop-metric or model gate request with no stop observed on its subject, with a subject index) and local_gate_runners_backfill (the ceiling and cursor of a one-time copy), and four triggers on claims that keep the first: one on a mechanical gate request's insert, one on a stop's insert, one on the delete of a gate request or a stop, and one on an update of id, subject, kind, origin or body. Other claims, the other runtime observations included, pass through them without a query. No schema-version change. The triggers and the ceiling, the newest claim they did not see, commit together in the store open; the gate requests at or below the ceiling are copied from 2 minutes after start, past the reconnect wave, 256 per background writer loan with a 50 ms pause, each re-checked for a stop under the writer. Until the copy completes the reconciler lists gate runners from the claims, as before.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; the table is local and never replicated or digested. Mixed-version safe: the triggers live in the database, so an older binary that writes claims keeps the table exact, and a newer one reads it.

compatibility.detail: No client, protocol or pairing changes. The reconciler sees the same gate runners as before.

downtime.detail: No added startup work: the one-time copy starts 2 minutes after the daemon does. Once it completes (minutes after the first start of this build), the reconciler's first pass after every start, and its full pass every 5 minutes, list gate runners from the table instead of a query that took 9.2 s on a busy member's store in the minute after a restart.

manual.detail: No operator actions or configuration changes; identity and stored state are preserved.

recovery.detail: Swapping back is supported: an older build reads the claims as before, and the triggers it keeps firing cost one indexed probe per gate request or runtime observation written.
